Seems mostly image search has been unfiltered. Content search (web search) relies on an index of pages (a database of urls + associated content that relate to keywords via an algorithm score). It would be very slow to change. Content looks at ancillary words and how closely those found in a page article related to the keyword(s) a user inputs.

In sum, if filters were dropped, the database for web search would be slower to change as more searches are conducted, users click-thru on those results (ie. 'vote' that the result is a good match for the search), and as new crawls process and contribute to the index of urls.

Just as you expect to slowly move up the organic web search results over time (1 to 3 mos) from when you create / improve page content, dropping filters would likely not see drastic web search changes for some time.
